normal.name: Pandottermon - The friend
normal.text: Every time I ask myself what I'm going to play for a new game because I'm looking for something that's colorful and fun but low stress but challenging just enough? I'm reminded that Stardew Valley exists.
I only just got into cozy farming games with Fields of Mistria and it is a great bedtime task game. Has me looking forward to Witchbrook as well!

normal.name: Jon 🎮
normal.text: Thinking of doing this too. I have to approve the game though 😂. I have PC and a brand new Switch 2 Please keep recommendations to like RPGs, JRPGs, souls-likes and action adventure games. I won’t play anything like platformers or cozy games

normal.name: Cameron
normal.text: Okay but what about that protein-folding game? What about learning games? Maybe relaxing and having fun is an accomplishment? Maybe *try* to understand something before talking out your ass.

normal.name: Sronmar—Coffee is Love
normal.text: I'd never played incremental games until this year. The closest I got before was maybe a couple of roguelikes, if that. It's weird because most of what I was into were RPG's, Soulslikes, Adventure games, ... They're simple games but very relaxing, at least I find them to be. Who enjoys them as well?

normal.name: Deny Ally
normal.text: New laptop + indie game backlog is a dangerous combo for the wallet, but honestly? Worth it for the cozy multiplayer nights.

normal.name: docvember
normal.text: it's people in 'bitch eating crackers' mode looking for reasons to complain because they're upset their articles aren't doing well. When I wrote my essay about wholesome games, one person was flipping out bragging about "I took AP poetry!" (wooow lmao. I have 3 degrees in arts and a minor in lit)

normal.name: docvember
normal.text: If the piece was just "hey, so, sometimes people feel weird about wholesome games. Why is that? Well, it's because one of the biggest audiences for wholesome games are members of the alt right" would slip off your brain like teflon. It's purely ideas, and humans don't retain ideas just via ideas.

normal.name: Cranmary Majora 🦃
normal.text: The more I play Stardew, the more I absolutely fucking HATE Marnie and I argue she’s the worst character in the game. Does nothing to help Shane. She never works, she just wanders around or stands in the kitchen. Mayor Lewis?!! Girl please.

normal.name: SandstormerArt
normal.text: Yeah! I also have that happening with music, TV and books. Just the other night I was going through things my parents would play on the car radio, and last week I was going watching old episodes of The Walking Dead because I followed it back then. There's something cozy about doing stuff like that.

normal.name: Holle
normal.text: Agreed! Making the reset a choice would probably make a game a bit lighter of tone. To go really grim, characters would be forced out of the cozy virtual realm into a body (they don’t need and maybe don’t want) and forced to do the dirty work of the overlords.

normal.name: 🍂 Bug 🍁
normal.text: Story driven games are the best, but No Man’s Sky scratches the “doing something useful simulator” itch for me because it *can* be like that but there’s just enough friction to getting things done that I have to put it down a lot sooner than games like Stardew Valley.
